Anya K: quick sync — I pushed the latest microbatch window changes to staging (micro_batch_interval_ms=4, coalesce_delay_ms=8, jitter_pct=15). seeing mixed results in the perf harness.
Ben R: saw that — overall qps up a bit, but 99p latency rose for some short-seq workloads. any profiling data yet?
Anya K: yes. attached a short snippet from the perf run + flame samples. main things: larger coalesced batches occasionally switch the kernel selection to the 'wide-kv' path which increases L2 pressure. also saw KV cache churn for sessions with many short requests.
Carlos M: interesting — can you paste the kernel selection log? would like to see the heuristic trigger thresholds.
Anya K: sure — from the runtime log: 
```
2026-11-03T14:12:03Z INFO kernel_selector: chosen=fast_multi_kernel reason="batch_size>=16 && kv_active==true"
2026-11-03T14:12:03Z DEBUG kernel_selector: fallback_candidate=single_stream_kernel cost_est=0.72
```
That "batch_size>=16" boundary is the culprit for some of our short-seq tails.
Devon S: so when coalesce makes a 16+ batch we hit multi-kernel path which is faster amortized, but for sequences of 8-16 tokens it pushes working set and causes extra KV evictions?
Anya K: exactly. our KV cache TTL is short in staging so when the kernel switches we do more KV fetches mid-inference causing ~6-12ms added 95/99 latency on some requests.
Priya L: do we see this only on mix workloads or also on pure chat short-turn workloads?
Ben R: primarily mixed — when short requests piggyback behind a slightly longer request in the same coalesce window. The coalesce delay=8ms setting lets that happen frequently.
Carlos M: potential mitigations: lower the coalesce delay to reduce cross-length mixing, or add a quick path that preserves kernel selection based on predicted max-seq in batch. Also jitter can help avoid synchronized alignments.
Anya K: I ran an A/B: jitter_pct=25, coalesce_delay_ms=6 vs baseline 8/15. With higher jitter we saw fewer large aligned batches and 99p latency dropped ~3.4% but p50 unchanged. qps dipped ~1.1%.
Devon S: small Q: where are token_budget targets in this config? do we cap tokens per-batch anywhere?
Anya K: we have a token_budget_target=512 per batch currently (soft). When the batch token sum exceeds this we break into sub-batches, but the heuristic runs after coalesce so it doesn't always prevent kernel switches.
Priya L: suggestion: move token_budget check into the coalescer pre-filter so we avoid forming batches that would cross the kernel threshold. That should reduce kernel path flips without entirely removing batching benefits.
Ben R: agree — also consider metric gating: if KV eviction rate > X, temporarily lower coalesce_delay or lower batch_size limit for that lane.
Carlos M: +1. Another angle: adjust kernel_selector to prefer the single-stream kernel when avg_seq_len < 12 even if batch_size>=16. That would keep working set smaller for short sequences.
Anya K: noted. I'll prototype two changes in staging: 1) pre-coalesce token_budget cap at 384, 2) kernel_selector tweak to bias single-stream for avg_seq_len < 12, 3) metric gate that raises jitter_pct to 30% when kv_eviction_rate > 0.02.
Devon S: for the metric gate, what's our latency for detection? we don't want oscillation. add a 30s smoothing window + min_activation_count=100.
Anya K: will do.
infra-bot: perf-run #482 finished — summary: baseline vs staging-v2: p50 -0.2%, p95 +1.1%, p99 +2.8%, kv_eviction_rate +0.018. Artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/482/*.svg
Priya L: thanks infra-bot. Next steps: land the pre-filter + selector tweak in feature branch, run the churn-sensitive workload and the PLT short-chat suite. If headroom remains, try raising token_budget_target incrementally.
Ben R: also log kernel_selector decision context (avg_seq_len, token_sum, kv_active, hw_mem_headroom) so we can correlate.
Anya K: will add more verbose selection logs behind a debug flag. planning to roll to canary after another run. target: keep p99 regression < 1% vs baseline while keeping qps within -2%.
Carlos M: sanity: update the console dashboard with kv_eviction_rate and kernel-path ration for the canary group so SRE can watch.
Anya K: adding those dash tiles now. thanks all — I’ll post results later today. :thumbsup:
